transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-02-14
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim, Priya Shah (Redwood); Samir Patel, Jenna Ortiz, Evan Liu (BrightHealth AI)
Summary: Demo focused on migration path from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood API. Covered API parity (params, streaming, function-calling), model mapping, embeddings transition, cost/latency tradeoffs, security (KMS, SSO, audit logs), and next steps to run benchmarks and share parity spreadsheet.

00:00 Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm alex from redwood, with priya our se, and today we're going to walk through how you'd map your current openai/anthropic/together usage to redwood's api and console. if there's anything you want us to dive deeper on, interrupt.
00:18 Samir: thanks alex, quick context — we've been on openai for chat completions, some anthopic for safety checks, and together for cheaper smaller model inference. our goals: cut cost a bit, maintain latency, and get better observability. also need to meet SOC2 requirements.
00:33 Priya: great, that's common. quick q: what's your typical sequence length and qps?
00:38 Jenna: typical sequence 512 tokens, peak qps around 40, p95 latency goal ~300ms for most interactive flows. cost is also a driver—embedding costs for search ops are non-trivial.
00:52 Priya: perfect. i'll start with an API parity overview — how common params map. redwood's text generation endpoint accepts both single-prompt and chat/message formats; we support temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop sequences, and streaming like openai. function-calling? yes we have structured output support and tool-calling primitives, though names differ slightly in the sdk.
01:16 Jenna: is there a one-to-one for function calling? we use that heavily.
01:20 Priya: mostly yes. for code, our sdk has a call_functions field and you can register json schema validators. watchouts: some model variants handle tool-calling differently — our docs call them "tool-friendly variants". i'll share examples.
01:33 Samir: how about model names — what would map to gpt-4 or claude?
01:37 Alex: good q, we maintain a curated model catalog. for example, if you're using openai:gpt-4, we'd recommend redwood/model-gpt4-v1 (hosted) or a pinned dedicated variant. for anthopic-like safety models, we have small safety classifiers you can chain. for smaller Together models we suggest our lightweight quantized variants (redwood/qt-small-v2) that are cheaper per-token. we'll send a spreadsheet with model-by-model parity and perf notes.
02:00 Evan: latency-wise, any expected regressions moving to redwood hosted?
02:04 Priya: typically we see comparable p50/p95 for same hardware; our runtime does continuous batching and prefix cache — sometimes p50 improves because of better batching, p95 depends on your distribution. for strict SLOs you can use Redwood Dedicated to guarantee capacity and lower variability.
02:22 Evan: and encryption? we need KMS/HSM keys for model input encryption at rest and customer-managed keys.
02:28 Alex: supported — VPC + private deployments include customer KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs; hosted supports CMKs for enterprise tiers. we'll map the specific controls in the security doc.
02:40 Jenna: what about tokenization differences — cost calc may change.
02:44 Priya: yes, tokenizer differences matter. tokens may count differently between models; part of the parity spreadsheet will include expected token delta and a recommended cost multiplier to estimate monthly spend. you should run your prompts through our tokenizer tool in the console; we provide a tokenizer endpoint and sample scripts.
03:00 Samir: embeddings — we use openai-embed-002 for semantic search. how's migration?
03:06 Priya: Redwood supports multiple embeddings backends and a unified embeddings endpoint. you can swap model names in the call, and we provide semantic similarity baselines. note: vector dimensions may differ — we include mapping and retraining guidance. for search you may need to reindex, and we recommend running a small A/B to compare recall/precision.
03:27 Jenna: any caveats on streaming vs chunked responses? we rely on streaming for perceived latency.
03:31 Priya: we support chunked server-sent and websocket streaming. function-calls can stream partial outputs; caveat: when you move to quantized models some streaming chunk sizes may be larger — small difference for UX but measurable.
03:46 Samir: let's talk about rate limits and burst policies. our traffic can spike.
03:50 Alex: hosted has tiered quotas and soft burst allowances; Dedicated offers reserved throughput and predictable latency. for our Hosted API we mention quotas and recommend a burst buffer or fallback model to keep SLA. Smart routing can tier requests from cheaper quantized models to heavier quality models if latency allows.
04:10 Jenna: how would we instrument this in your console?
04:13 Priya: Redwood Console has per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, traces, and error analysis. you can set rollout policies (canary, A/B) and automatic fallback. we'll demo the console in a follow-up or send screenshots.
04:27 Evan: security/compliance again — SSO, RBAC, audit logs — all mandatory.
04:30 Alex: yes, SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, fine-grain RBAC, and immutable audit logs are available for enterprise plans. Private deployment includes extra controls.
04:40 (brief cross-talk)
04:45 Priya: demo time — i'll show a migration snippet. first the openai call we see: curl -X POST https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions -H Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_KEY with messages, temperature, max_tokens. equivalent in redwood: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY with messages, temperature, max_new_tokens. small differences: param names (max_tokens -> max_new_tokens), stop sequences handled similarly. streaming uses chunked=1.
05:20 Priya: here's a sample node sdk snippet for function calling — we pass tools array and a call_functions flag, and the response includes a tool_call object. translation is about 80% mechanical. i'll paste examples into the follow-up email.
05:40 Samir: what about billing units — per-token billing alignment? we bill per-generation token + prompt token similar to others, but we have separate units for embeddings. price points vary by model; we'll include estimated per-million token numbers.
06:00 Jenna: are there any breaking changes for chat state / multi-turn?
06:04 Priya: we support KV cache and session tokens; to preserve multi-turn you can persist message history or use the kv cache API for low-latency continuation. some models have different context window sizes; check the parity doc for window sizes.
06:20 Samir: can we run a quick benchmark? sample workload: 512-token prompts, 40 qps, 95th latency target 300ms.
06:26 Alex: yes we can — priya will provision a dedicated mini-cluster to run that and provide results. we'll also run the same prompts against your current openai key to get apples-to-apples.
06:40 Priya: a couple of migration gotchas: 1) tokenization differences that affect cost; 2) embeddings dimension mismatch; 3) function-calling schema validation differences; 4) different default stop token behavior. all manageable but need test harness.
06:58 Jenna: any examples of customers who migrated?
07:02 Alex: we've done migrations for two fintechs and an ecommerce search team; typical first phase is parity mapping + a small pilot, then rollouts with canaries. i'll share case studies.
07:20 Evan: regarding private deployment, network egress and data residency — can we keep everything in our VPC?
07:25 Alex: yes private deployment supports customer VPC and on-prem package. for hosted we have region controls. we'll map options in the next doc.
07:40 Samir: about observability — can we tag requests by tenant/route for cost attribution?
07:44 Priya: yes, per-request metadata tags and per-token attribution. Console shows cost per-route and you can export token-level billing.
07:55 Jenna: SDKs — do you have python/js/java parity?
07:58 Alex: python and node are first-class, java go is in beta. we provide direct curl/HTTP examples.
08:08 (short silence, typing)
08:15 Samir: any legal/procurement concerns — we have a procurement checklist.
08:18 Alex: we accept PO, we have standard t&c for enterprise, and for Private deployments there are licensing terms. procurement will get the security/compliance pack.
08:30 Priya: closing the demo, we'll send: parity spreadsheet, sample snippets, trial credentials, security docs, and propose dates for the deep dive.
08:40 Jenna: sounds good. one more q: can you run embeddings migration and report delta in recall?
08:45 Priya: yes we'll run an A/B on a sample index and report recall/precision numbers plus latency/cost.
08:52 Samir: awesome. thanks.
08:55 Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with those artifacts and schedule the deep dive. meeting ends.

Notes and transcript quirks: occasional mis-heard words and punctuation; some product names transcribed as "redwood/model-gpt4-v1" though internal names may differ. references to Together and Anthropic spelled/talked informally (anthopic, anthorpic) in parts of the recording.
